work_order.understanding:
Issue #72 collects six follow-ups from the review and QA of PR #69 (for #42): five review findings (forecast as a fourth reader of the occurrence stamp on the wrong split type; a test case whose name claims to pin the guard it does not pin; a raw-SQL test helper whose justification is false; a release note missing from files[]; a missing [AI] PR title prefix) and one QA defect (unsplitting a posted schedule payment destroys it). plan/critique.json is {} so there were nothing to judge; I re-derived the findings against this tree rather than inheriting the proposal's conclusions. All six hold.

This round exists because the previous plan was REJECTED on one point, and the plan is rebuilt around it. v2's unsplit fix guarded the parent's deletion by summing the children the user SELECTED (newNonChildTransactions). That is the wrong set: at transactions.ts:468-474, when exactly one child remains, the existing code already appends that remaining child to nonChildTransactionsToUpdate, so the rows that will exist afterwards are the promoted set, not the selected one. On a filled two-child split (parent 12345, children 5000/7345) with only the first selected, the selected sum is 5000, short of 12345, so v2 collapsed a correctly filled split into one 12345 parent carrying the selected child's category and deleted BOTH children — one never selected. Reachable: 'Unsplit 1 transactions' only requires selected rows to be a parent or child (useTransactionRowContextActions.ts:122, SelectedTransactionsButton.tsx:191). v2's own test for this used THREE children, where remainingChildTransactions.length === 2 makes deleteParentTransaction false and the new branch is never entered.

The corrected rule builds the condition over nonChildTransactionsToUpdate. I transcribed today's function verbatim into a scratch harness, wrote the corrected rule beside it, and ran both over thirteen parent/child shapes. The corrected rule is IDENTICAL to today on every shape where the promoted set accounts for the parent — including both shapes the rejection names — and diverges only on never-filled and partially-typed splits, where today's code destroys the parent's amount.

The other five findings are unchanged. The forecast passes getTransactions' result, which carries splits:'inline' (forecast-filters.ts:83), as buildFutureScheduleOccurrences' fifth argument, and that array is indexed by indexPostedScheduleTransactions; any split type but 'all' appends is_parent = 0 (executors.ts:238-244), so the inline set cannot see a split parent — and splitTransaction keeps schedule/schedule_occurrence on the row it makes a parent while makeChild copies neither onto children, so the split parent is the ONLY stamped row. A posted-and-split occurrence is invisible to its own posted-check and is projected twice. Display-only: it cannot double-pay, which is the guard #69 fixed. getPostedScheduleTransactionsQuery (shared/schedules.ts:251) already passes splits:'all' and returns exactly the three-column shape the consumers are typed on.

The brief's earlier rejection of AC-7/AC-8 (browser criteria nothing in the product can decide) is honoured: both stay out of acceptance[] and live in qa_script and out_of_scope.
work_order.root_cause:
Two independent defects sharing one shape: a consumer reads the (schedule, schedule_occurrence) stamp, or a transaction's amount, off a row set the default query shape cannot see.

The forecast reads the stamp off getTransactions' result, which passes splits:'inline' and excludes split parents — the only rows carrying the stamp, since splitTransaction keeps schedule/schedule_occurrence on the row it makes a parent and makeChild copies neither onto children. getPostedScheduleTransactionsQuery already passes splits:'all' and returns the three-column shape the consumers are typed on; the forecast is the fourth reader and the only one left on the default split type.

Unsplit: makeAsNonChildTransactions decides to delete the parent from the CHILD COUNT rather than from whether the rows replacing it account for it. A split opened from the register starts as two 0.00 children, so the count says 'safe' while the amounts say the parent is the only row carrying any value — and the occurrence stamp with it. The single-child branch at :452 already implements the correct behaviour; the general branch does not extend it.

For anyone re-deriving this: the set that replaces the parent is nonChildTransactionsToUpdate (:468-474) — the selected children PLUS the remaining child whenever remainingChildTransactions.length === 1. Any amount-based guard must be built over that set. Building it over the selected children alone misreads the shape a filled split takes when the user unsplits one child of two, and collapses a correctly filled split.
work_order.approach:
Four code/test changes plus two release notes. Every claim carrying a number was measured on this tree; scratch harnesses deleted afterwards, tree clean.

A. FORECAST (finding 1). In forecast/app.ts import aqlQuery from '#server/aql' and, from '#shared/schedules', getPostedScheduleTransactionsQuery and the PostedScheduleTransaction type; after schedules is filtered, fetch the posted-schedule-transactions query and pass it as the fifth argument to buildFutureScheduleOccurrences in place of transactions. transactions still goes to projectForecastData untouched and MUST stay on the inline split set — there the CHILDREN carry the amounts the projection sums. Widening it double-counts every split; the existing test 'does not double-count split parents in posted transaction balances' (app.test.ts:492) is that guard. Retype the postedTransactions parameter to PostedScheduleTransaction[] and ADD the type import — without it the file does not compile. The retype is DOCUMENTATION, not a guard: TransactionEntity is structurally assignable to PostedScheduleTransaction, so passing the inline set back would still typecheck; the tests pin the behaviour.

B. UNSPLIT (finding 2) — CORRECTED, this is the rejection. After nonChildTransactionsToUpdate and deleteParentTransaction exist, sum the PROMOTED set with the file's existing num helper: if deleteParentTransaction AND that total differs from the parent's amount, return the parent through makeTransactionWithChildCategory (with error: null) and delete childTransactions. Summing nonChildTransactionsToUpdate rather than newNonChildTransactions is the whole correction: when remainingChildTransactions.length === 1 that array already contains the remaining child, so a filled split whose children sum to the parent passes and falls through to today's correct split-out. A ?? parentTransaction fallback covers the only arity where newNonChildTransactions is empty (unreachable from Account.tsx:1262, but without it the call throws). This must return the parent THROUGH makeTransactionWithChildCategory, not merely narrow the boolean — I tried the cheaper version in the harness: it leaves is_parent: true with a spread of the parent, a split parent with no children, worse than today's bug. error: null clears the stale SplitTransactionError.

Thirteen shapes run against today's function side by side. SAME on: filled 12345=5000+7345 unsplit-all; filled 12345=5000+7345 ONE selected (the rejection's shape, keeps today's two-row split-out); filled 8345=4000+4345 ONE selected; filled 12345=4000+4000+4345 one selected (remaining 2, branch not entered, parent reduced to 8345); four children with two selected (parent reduced to 6345, nothing deleted); zero-amount parent with no children; the single-child early return at :452. CHANGE only on: 12345 with 0/0 unsplit-all (the QA defect); the same split with one child selected; 12345 with 5000/0; three-child 5000/4000/0 with two selected; and 2000/1500 single child not selected. Every CHANGE is a shape where today's code loses money; no SAME shape moves.

C. TEST FRAMING (finding 3). Rename 'leaves the status queries agreeing with the guard after a split' to 'still reports a split-parented occurrence as posted' and replace its guard-pinning comment with a pointer to the sibling that actually pins it. No assertion changes. Confirmed by execution: reverting the guard's splits:'all' gives 1 failed | 51 passed, the failure being the sibling, while the renamed case passes.

D. TEST IDIOM (finding 4). Replace readSplitFamily's body with the AQL query keeping the id/parent_id $or. The inline type literal, the v_transactions_internal reference and the 20170102-integer detour go away; the false-justification comment is deleted rather than rewritten. The select list MUST include 'schedule'. Two assertion-convention changes are REQUIRED: is_parent comes back boolean not 1, and schedule/schedule_occurrence come back undefined not null — without toMatchObject is_parent: true and toBeFalsy() the rewrite fails on 'expected undefined to be null'. Applied with them: 52/52.

E. RELEASE NOTES. Two. The forecast correction folds into the existing schedule-occurrence note; the unsplit fix gets its own note, because it is NOT schedule-specific — unsplitting any never-filled split destroys the row's amount, schedule or not.

Not splitting the ticket: two views of one interaction, and the wider-reaching one is not the smaller one.

files.change: Import aqlQuery from '#server/aql' and, from '#shared/schedules', getPostedScheduleTransactionsQuery and the PostedScheduleTransaction type. After schedules is filtered (:127-131), add the posted-schedule-transactions query and pass it as the fifth argument to buildFutureScheduleOccurrences (:141-147) in place of transactions. transactions continues to projectForecastData unchanged and must stay on the inline split set — there the children carry the amounts the projection sums.
files.why: Fix for finding 1. getTransactions' inline split set cannot see a split parent, the only row carrying the occurrence stamp, so a posted-and-split occurrence is invisible to isScheduleOccurrencePosted and gets projected a second time. getPostedScheduleTransactionsQuery already passes splits:'all' and returns exactly the three-column shape indexPostedScheduleTransactions expects.

files.change: Retype buildFutureScheduleOccurrences' postedTransactions parameter (:187) from TransactionEntity[] to PostedScheduleTransaction[] and ADD import type { PostedScheduleTransaction } from '#shared/schedules'; alongside the existing #shared/schedules import (:8-14) — without the import the file does not compile. Drop TransactionEntity only if unused (it is still used for simulatedTransactions, so it should not). No logic change. Comment the parameter to say the narrow type documents the three-column projection and is NOT a guard.
files.why: The parameter now receives a three-column projection rather than whole transaction rows, and the wide typing was looser than the use. The comment exists because the narrow type looks like it prevents the bug's return and does not — the tests are what pin it.

files.change: In makeAsNonChildTransactions, immediately after const deleteParentTransaction = remainingChildTransactions.length <= 1; (:476) — i.e. AFTER nonChildTransactionsToUpdate exists — sum the PROMOTED set: const promotedTotal = nonChildTransactionsToUpdate.map(t => num(t.amount)).reduce((total, amount) => total + amount, 0); using the file's existing num helper (:41). Then guard: if (deleteParentTransaction && promotedTotal !== num(parentTransaction.amount)) return { updated: [{ ...makeTransactionWithChildCategory(parentTransaction, newNonChildTransactions[0] ?? parentTransaction), error: null }], deleted: childTransactions }. When the promoted set does account for the parent, fall through unchanged. Return the parent THROUGH makeTransactionWithChildCategory — do not merely narrow the boolean, which leaves is_parent: true and is worse than today. The ?? parentTransaction fallback covers the arity where newNonChildTransactions is empty (unreachable from Account.tsx:1262, but without it the call throws). Add a comment naming the invariant: a parent may only be deleted when the rows replacing it account for it.
files.why: Fix for finding 2, and the correction the rejection demands. The set that will exist after the unsplit is nonChildTransactionsToUpdate (:468-474) — the selected children PLUS the remaining child whenever exactly one remains — NOT newNonChildTransactions. Summing the selected set collapses a filled two-child split when the user unsplits one child, deleting both children including one never selected; summing the promoted set keeps today's correct split-out there while still fixing the QA defect. error: null clears a stale SplitTransactionError the spread would carry onto a row no longer part of a split.

files.change: Comment only, at :586-597. The block explains that splits:'all' is required for the post guard and names getHasTransactionsQuery and getPostedScheduleTransactionsQuery as consumers that already pass it. Extend it to name the forecast as the fourth reader, now corrected.
files.why: No behaviour change — the guard itself is correct and was fixed by #69. A stale list of the correct readers is how the forecast reading drifted in the first place.

(i) Rename 'leaves the status queries agreeing with the guard after a split' to 'still reports a split-parented occurrence as posted' and rewrite its comment to say what it asserts, pointing at the sibling 'writes no second transaction when the posted one has been split'. No assertion changes. (ii) Replace readSplitFamily's body (:1566) with the AQL query — q('transactions').options({ splits: 'all' }).filter({ $or: [{ id: parentId }, { parent_id: parentId }] }).select(['id','is_parent','parent_id','schedule','schedule_occurrence']) — returning data. cases: does not re-project a posted occurrence whose transaction has been split — post a weekly occurrence through the real handlers, split the posted row, give the two children half the amount each; assert the occurrence's data point has an empty transactions array and the running balance counts the real rows once. Today the point carries a projected entry of the full amount and the balance is too low from that date on.
keeps projecting the next occurrence after a split — control arm pinning that the fix removes the duplicate rather than all projection for a split-posted schedule.

the existing 'does not double-count split parents in posted transaction balances' (app.test.ts:492) continues to pass — it is the guard that transactions must stay on the inline split set, and widening it is the rejected alternative.

unsplitting a split whose children were never filled in keeps the parent and its amount — 12345 stamped parent with two 0.00 children, unsplit both: one updated row at 12345 with is_parent: false, both children deleted, nothing at 0. The reproduced QA defect. Assert is_parent: false explicitly: narrowing only the boolean leaves the row a split parent.

unsplitting that same parent leaves the occurrence stamp on the surviving row — the row still carries schedule and schedule_occurrence, which keeps /schedules reading Paid instead of Due. Asserted directly rather than inferred from the amount.
the surviving row carries no stale SplitTransactionError — the promoted row's error is null, so the row is not rendered with a split error against an amount that is present.

unsplitting a FILLED split still splits it out — 12345 parent with children 5000 and 7345, unsplit both: two updated children at their own amounts, parent deleted. Guards against the fix over-reaching into correctly-filled splits.

unsplitting ONE child of a filled two-child split still splits it out — 12345 parent with children 5000 and 7345, unsplit the first only: two updated rows at 5000 and 7345, parent deleted, nothing else touched. THIS IS THE REGRESSION TEST FOR THE REJECTION. The previous guard summed the SELECTED children (5000) instead of the promoted set (5000+7345), read that as a mismatch, and returned a single 12345 parent carrying the selected child's category with both children deleted. Expected values are identical to today's function; assert them literally so the case fails if the guard moves back onto the selected set.

unsplitting one child of a filled split whose amounts are 4000/4345 under an 8345 parent also still splits it out — same shape, different numbers, to catch a guard comparing only the selected total against the parent. Expect 4000 and 4345, parent deleted.

unsplitting one child of a filled THREE-child split still leaves the parent — 12345 parent with children 4000/4000/4345, unsplit the first: parent survives at 8345 with the promoted child alongside, nothing deleted. This is the case the previous plan listed for this property and it cannot catch the regression (remainingChildTransactions.length === 2 makes deleteParentTransaction false, so the new branch is never entered). Kept as a second arm, not as the arm that catches it.

unsplitting two of three partially-typed children keeps the parent at its full amount — 12345 parent with children 5000/4000/0, unsplit the first two: the parent survives at 12345. Pins the rule this fix adopts so the choice is visible rather than incidental.

the existing case 'writes no second transaction when the posted one has been split' continues to pass and remains the one that fails when the guard's splits:'all' is reverted — the rename in finding 3 must not move that coverage onto the renamed case. Verified by execution: reverting the guard gives exactly 1 failed | 51 passed, the failure being that sibling.

readSplitFamily reads the split family through AQL: the helper issues a q('transactions') query with splits:'all' and an $or over id/parent_id, and neither it nor the assertion below mentions v_transactions_internal or a 20170102 integer. Suite passes at 52/52 with these edits — verified by applying them.

Case (b) is the one the previous plan broke — its guard summed the SELECTED children (5000), read that as short of 12345, and returned a single 12345 parent with the selected child's category, having deleted both children including the one never selected. acceptance.check: The test case reporting a split-parented occurrence as posted is named for what it asserts, and the guard it used to claim to pin is pinned by the sibling case instead.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Read the case in packages/loot-core/src/server/schedules/app.test.ts: name and comment must not claim agreement with the guard and must point at 'writes no second transaction when the posted one has been split'. qa_script: Boot the demo budget via 'View demo' on the initial setup screen (after 'Don't use a server') — an empty budget has no schedules to exercise the schedule cases.

AC-3 first, since it is the one with visible data loss: add a one-off schedule (payee QA Unsplit Then Post, account Bank of America, amount 123.45, date a few days out). Post it from the row's actions menu ('Post transaction', not '…today'). In the register select the posted row, click its Category cell, choose Split, leave both new rows at 0.00. Right-click the split and choose 'Unsplit 1 transactions'. Expect the 123.45 row to remain standing alone with its schedule badge and no split error, and the two 0.00 rows gone. Check /schedules: the occurrence must still read Paid and its preview row must be gone. Before the fix the 123.45 row disappears entirely, only the 0.00 rows remain, and /schedules reads Due with the preview row back.

AC-4 immediately after, on a split before it is unsplit: enter 50.00 and 73.45 into the two children, then 'Unsplit 1 transactions'. Expect two separate rows of 50.00 and 73.45 and no 123.45 parent. On the unsplit row, also confirm it behaves as an ordinary transaction (no split affordance, no 'Unassigned amount' error) rather than as a leftover split parent.

Then the arm AC-4's second clause names, and the one the previous plan got wrong: re-split a 123.45 row, enter 50.00 and 73.45, right-click ONE of the two children and unsplit only that one. Expect two separate rows of 50.00 and 73.45, no 123.45 parent, and the child you did not select still present. The previous implementation returned a single 12345 row here and had deleted both children.

AC-1: add a weekly schedule on Checking for -100. Let one occurrence post, then split the posted register row and give the two children -50.00 each. Open the balance forecast (Reports > Overview) over a window covering that occurrence and the next. Expect NO projected entry on the occurrence's day and the balance counting the real rows once; the following week's occurrence must still be projected. Before the fix a projected -100 sits on top of the real -100 and the balance is 100 too low.

The partially-typed case, which is a visible change and is not in the ticket's repro: split a 123.45 row, type 50.00 into ONE child and leave the other empty, then unsplit both. Expect one row at 123.45 and the typed 50.00 gone. That is the rule this fix adopts; confirm it, and report it in the PR description rather than letting a reviewer find it.

At PR time, not in the browser: confirm the PR title begins with '[AI] ' per .github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md (#69's did not, nor did 71, 68, 67 or 65), and that both upcoming-release-notes/fix-unsplit-empty-split.md and the edited fix-split-occurrence-double-post.md appear in files[] along with every other changed path.
risks: The partially-typed split semantics are a product judgement, not a derivation from the code. A parent with children 5000/4000/0 is kept at its full 12345 and the typed 9000 is discarded; today the parent is reduced to the typed amounts and 2345 is lost instead. Both sides lose money on that shape. If a maintainer decides the typed partials should win, the condition narrows to a children-sum-of-zero test and nothing else in the order moves. Pinned by a test, in qa_script, and named here as the one place a maintainer may overrule.

The guard fires on child count as well as amount, so when the children do NOT account for the parent, unsplitting any subset of them dissolves the WHOLE split: every child is deleted, including ones the user did not select, and the parent survives standing alone at its own amount. The money outcome is the safe one — verified on all thirteen shapes, every divergence from today is a shape where today's code destroys value — but the behaviour is visible. This is CORRECTED from the previous plan's wording, which scoped the dissolution to 'a never-filled split' and asserted the money outcome was right only on the three-child shapes; with the guard built over the promoted set it applies to every never-filled or partially-typed split regardless of how many children the user selected. A reviewer should confirm that reads as intentional.

Clearing the promoted parent's error is a scope judgement, not something the ticket asked for. The consequence of not doing it is a stale SplitTransactionError on the returned row. Reachability is narrower than an earlier draft claimed: the desktop register's hasSplitError in TransactionsTable.tsx:2767 gates on trans.is_parent || trans.is_child, and the promoted row has is_parent: false with no is_child, so the desktop badge would NOT render. The mobile editor (TransactionEdit.tsx:306) checks only transaction.error?.type === 'SplitTransactionError' with no such gate, so it WOULD show a split action against a row with a correct amount. Clearing it is still right — the value is a persisted json column (server/aql/schema/index.ts:47) — but the visible symptom is mobile-only.

The added AQL query on the forecast's hot path is unmeasured. Correctness was verified; latency was not, and there is no benchmark in the repo for this handler. It mirrors what useSchedules already runs.

The retype in forecast-schedules.ts is documentation, not a guard — TransactionEntity is structurally assignable to PostedScheduleTransaction, so the inline set could be passed back and would still compile. The tests are what hold the fix; do not let a reviewer read the narrow type as enforcement.
The release-note split is a judgement call a maintainer may reverse by merging the two note bodies.

This order changes no file under .sdlc/**, .github/**, docs/spec/**, docs/prd.md, docs/trd.md or docs/ui.md. The one place the plan would have liked to is .github/** — wiring release-notes-check.mjs into a workflow so release-note front matter became a machine-checked gate — and it is left out deliberately; see out_of_scope.
out_of_scope: Retitling PR #69 to carry the [AI] prefix — a one-word change to a merged PR's title, not a code change, so it cannot appear in files[], and editing another PR's title is outward-facing. Recorded in qa_script for this PR's own title and in residual_risks; deliberately not an AC, per the brief's earlier rejection.

Wiring release-notes-check.mjs into a CI workflow so release-note front matter becomes a machine-checked gate. That is a change to .github/**, which no ticket here may touch, and is repo policy rather than a fix for #72.
Making the schedule stamp survive an unsplit by re-stamping the promoted children — a design question about what the stamp means, not a follow-up to this defect.
E2E coverage for the unsplit path; there is no Playwright test for the register's 'Unsplit' action today. Unit cases plus browser checks cover the reported defect.
The other consumers of getTransactions — they are balance uses and want the children.
Whether the forecast should itemise a split-parented occurrence's children as separate projected rows rather than suppressing the projection.
work_order.confidence_rationale:
The rejection in plan/brief.md was one objection, and it was correct: v2's guard summed the children the user SELECTED, while the rows that will exist after the unsplit are nonChildTransactionsToUpdate -- the selection PLUS the remaining child whenever exactly one remains, at transactions.ts:468-474. I did not take the proposal's word for the correction; I transcribed today's makeAsNonChildTransactions verbatim into a harness, wrote both candidate rules beside it, and ran all three over thirteen parent/child shapes. The rejected rule diverges from today's shipped behaviour on both shapes the rejection names (12345 with 5000/7345 one selected, and 8345 with 4000/4345 one selected) -- collapsing a correctly filled split into one parent with both children deleted -- and the corrected rule is identical to today on those and on every other shape where the promoted set accounts for the parent. It diverges only on never-filled and partially-typed splits, which is the class of shape where today's code destroys the parent's amount. I then went further than the proposal and could not: I applied the corrected rule to the REAL module (not a copy), added the two regression cases the rejection demanded, and confirmed they pass 22/22; re-pointing the guard back at the selected set makes exactly those two cases fail with 'expected [[p,12345]] to deeply equal [[c1,5000],[c2,7345]]', so the regression is pinned in both directions. Full loot-core suite with the fix: 87 files, 1271 passed, 1 expected fail, 2 skipped, exit 0. I also closed the one gap the proposal left open: I applied fix A to the forecast and ran it (4 files, 22/22) plus yarn typecheck green across all ten workspaces -- the proposal had recorded this as an unknown on the grounds that source files were not editable in its environment; they are editable here, so that unknown was an artefact of its sandbox rather than a property of the change, and it is now closed rather than carried forward. Every one of the six findings is now backed by execution on this tree.

What still holds it at 90 rather than higher is one genuine judgement, not a verification gap: the partially-typed split (children 5000/4000/0 under a 12345 parent) keeps the parent at full amount and discards the typed 9000, where today keeps 9000 and loses 2345. Both sides lose money; I measured both. That is a product decision the code does not settle, and it is pinned by a test, named in qa_script and named as the one place a maintainer may overrule, with the one-line fallback written down. alternatives_considered.approach: Sum the children the user SELECTED (newNonChildTransactions) rather than the promoted set — the previous plan's rule, restated because it is the rejected one and the difference is the whole point of this round.

When remainingChildTransactions.length === 1 the function already appends that remaining child to nonChildTransactionsToUpdate, so those are the rows that will exist afterwards; the selected set is not a subset of the future state but a different, smaller set. On a filled 12345 split with children 5000/7345 and only the first selected, the selected sum is 5000, the guard fires, and the result is one 12345 parent carrying the selected child's category with BOTH children deleted — a correctly filled split collapsed by the fix meant to protect it, on the most common register action, deleting a row the user never selected. Measured against today's function on thirteen shapes, this rule diverges from today on exactly the shapes that must not move.

alternatives_considered.approach: Guard on the children summing to zero rather than on summing to the parent — only rescue the never-filled case, and let a partially-typed split behave as it does today.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The narrower rule, considered seriously because it changes least. It leaves the partially-typed shape (5000/4000/0 under 12345) destroying 2345 of the parent's value — the same class of defect as the QA report: a parent deleted while rows that do not account for it replace it. It is the exact fallback if the maintainer judgement recorded in risks goes the other way, and it is one line. Not adopted by default because the QA report is about money disappearing on unsplit, and 'the children sum to zero' is a proxy for 'the user never typed anything' rather than the invariant the fix needs — that the parent may only be deleted when the rows replacing it account for it.

alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Unsplitting is a user-initiated revert of a split they made moments earlier, and the register already shows the split error on the row. Blocking moves the problem rather than fixing it and leaves the count-vs-amount decision in place.

work_order.debate_summary:
There was no critique to judge -- for the second round running. plan/critique.json is {} again, so the critic has written nothing in two consecutive rounds and the council has had no review voice in either. I say that plainly because a summary presenting tidy consensus would misrepresent what happened. The arbitration that actually mattered was the recorded REJECTION in plan/brief.md, and the proposal is built around answering it.

On that rejection: it was correct, and v3 answers it properly rather than arguing around it. v2's guard summed the children the user SELECTED; the rows that will exist after the unsplit are nonChildTransactionsToUpdate -- the selection PLUS the remaining child whenever exactly one remains, twenty lines above where the guard goes (transactions.ts:468-474). So on a filled two-child split with one child right-clicked, the selected sum is 5000 against a 12345 parent, the guard fires, and a correctly filled split collapses into a single 12345 parent carrying the selected child's category with BOTH children deleted. I verified the mechanism in the source and then reproduced the outcome in my own harness. I also confirmed the previous plan's test could not have caught it: its three-child case leaves remainingChildTransactions.length at 2, so deleteParentTransaction is false and the new branch is never entered.

I did not simply accept v3's correction, because a plan that answers a rejection by describing the right set is not the same as a plan whose right set has been exercised. So I applied the corrected guard to the REAL module -- not a copy, which is all the proposal could do -- added the two cases the rejection required, and got 22/22. Then I re-pointed the sum back at the selected set and confirmed exactly those two cases fail. That is the property the rejection asked for, verified in both directions rather than asserted.

What I rejected from the proposal, explicitly: its route_request. It asked to insert a qa stage, but state/72.json's planned_route is already plan -> implement -> review -> qa -- QA is on it. Asking for a stage already granted is not a signal, so the field is omitted rather than passed on.

What I corrected: the proposal recorded, in both unknowns and residual_risks, that it could not apply fix A or re-run the forecast suite 'because source files were not editable in this environment', and it asked a future implementer to re-run its thirteen shapes against the edited module for the same reason. I probed the claim -- a write into packages/loot-core/src/shared/ succeeds -- applied fix A, ran the forecast suite (22/22) and yarn typecheck (green across all ten workspaces), applied the unsplit guard to the real module and ran the full loot-core suite (1271 passed, exit 0). Both of those reservations were artefacts of the proposer's sandbox, not risks in the change, and I have closed them instead of passing them on as work for someone else. Worth recording as a process observation: a council member's tooling limitations should not become the next stage's to-do list.

What I did NOT overturn, having re-derived it: the forecast diagnosis (chain re-read end to end -- the inline splits option, the is_parent = 0 predicate, the parameter reaching indexPostedScheduleTransactions and nothing else, and splitTransaction keeping the stamp on the parent while makeChild copies neither field); findings 3 and 4, whose code I confirmed still stands and whose fixes were measured at 52/52 last round; and the decision not to split the ticket -- two views of one interaction, and the wider-reaching one is not the smaller one.

The honest weak spot, not tidied: the partially-typed split rule remains a judgement rather than a derivation. It keeps the parent at 12345 and discards the typed 9000, where today keeps 9000 and loses 2345 -- I measured both sides and each loses money. It is pinned by a test, called out in qa_script, and named as the one place a maintainer may overrule, with the one-line fallback (guard on a zero sum) written down. Second honest weak spot: the fifth query added to the forecast's hot path is unmeasured for latency and the repo has no benchmark for it. Third: clearing the promoted row's error targets a mobile-only symptom, so the desktop-badge justification in the earlier draft was wrong even though clearing the field is right -- risks and residual_risks both say so now.

And the finding that should worry the council most: a critic that produced nothing in two consecutive rounds has not reviewed this plan at all. My confidence is high because I re-derived and re-measured the load-bearing claims myself, not because anything else checked them.
residual_risks: The partially-typed split semantics are a product judgement and this is where the change is both visible and lossy — see risks. Measured both sides: with the fix 12345 survives and the typed 9000 is discarded; today 9000 survives and 2345 is lost. The case is in qa_script so it is checked and reported rather than discovered by a reviewer.

The guard dissolves a whole split whenever the children do not account for the parent, so unsplitting only some children of a never-filled or partially-typed split deletes the ones not selected too. The money outcome is the safe one on every shape measured, but the behaviour is visible; a reviewer should confirm it reads as intentional. The previous plan understated this by scoping it to 'a never-filled split'; it is restated in risks.

The stale-error fix targets a mobile-only symptom (see risks). If a reviewer reads the desktop badge as the reason, the justification is wrong even though clearing the field is right — the value is persisted and the mobile editor renders it ungated.
The added AQL query on the forecast's hot path is unmeasured for latency; a budget with many schedules may read more rows than the old path.

The [AI] prefix omission is systemic across pipeline-authored PRs 65, 67, 68, 69 and 71, and nothing in this order fixes the pipeline that produced the other four. It is a qa_script step rather than an acceptance criterion because no browser run and no existing CI case can decide it — the same reason release-note contents are not an AC. If the pipeline's PR-creation step is the real defect, that is a maintainer-stage change, not part of #72.
The caller sweep for makeAsNonChildTransactions covered packages/ excluding node_modules; a consumer reaching it through a generated or dynamic import path would not have appeared.

The three-child register affordance — the Category-cell split versus the right-click 'Unsplit N transactions' item — is exercised only by unit tests; QA's repro and the browser checks use two children.

A critic produced no findings in two consecutive rounds (plan/critique.json is {} both times), so no council member has reviewed this plan's reasoning. My confidence rests entirely on my own re-derivation and measurement. If that re-derivation shares a blind spot with the proposal's — and both were built by reading the same files — nothing in this process would have caught it.

The forecast's new split-occurrence unit test is specified by shape but not by recipe; if it turns out to be impractical to drive the real handlers with currentDay() pinned inside app.test.ts, the forecast fix could land with only AC-1's browser pass covering it. AC-2 requires a failing test when the fix is reverted, so this must be resolved rather than deferred.

Evidence: work-order.json files[2] specifies verbatim `const promotedTotal = nonChildTransactionsToUpdate.map(t => num(t.amount)).reduce((total, amount) => total + amount, 0);` and `if (deleteParentTransaction && promotedTotal !== num(parentTransaction.amount))`, and root_cause names the invariant: "a parent may only be deleted when the rows replacing it account for it." transactions.ts:496-500 ships `promotedRowsAreAllZero` instead. Driving the real `makeAsNonChildTransactions` (probe deleted after): parent 12345 with children 5000/0, unsplitting both -> `updated [c0:5000, c1:0]`, `deleted [p:12345]` (7345 destroyed); the same split with only the typed child selected -> identical. Parent 12345 with children 5000/-5000 (net zero), unsplitting both -> `updated [c0:5000, c1:-5000]`, `deleted [p:12345]` (surviving rows net 0 against a 12345 parent). Under the work order's rule all three keep the parent at 12345. Positive-arm control: filled 12345 = 5000/7345 gives `updated [c0:5000, c1:7345]`, `deleted [p:12345]` under both rules; negative never-filled -12345/0/0 keeps the parent at -12345. The deviation is deliberate and argued in the comment at :492-495 and pinned by the test at transactions.test.ts:621, which asserts `deleted: [['p', 12345]]` for 5000/4000/0 — the 2345 is dropped. work-order.json risks[0] anticipates this overrule but requires it be surfaced: qa_script[5] says to 'split a 123.45 row, type 50.00 into ONE child and leave the other empty, then unsplit both. Expect one row at 123.45 and the typed 50.00 gone.' Under this PR QA gets two rows of 50.00 and 0.00. The overshoot reasoning is sound for sums ABOVE the parent; the same rule also fires when the promoted sum is BELOW it, which is the case the ticket exists for.

Fix: Adopt the work order's sum test, or — if the overrule is accepted — keep `every(... === 0)` but also fire when the promoted total is BELOW the parent's amount, so the 5000/0 and 5000/-5000 shapes keep the parent. At minimum, amend qa_script[5] in the PR description to state what QA will actually observe.

Fix: Apply the same emptiness test to the branch that rewrites the parent's amount: when the remaining children are all 0.00, leave the parent's `amount` alone instead of replacing it with their sum. Alternatively file a follow-up — but then say so in the PR description, because the guard's comment reads as a statement of the general invariant and it is not one.

Evidence: `gh pr diff 81 --name-only` returns 9 paths; `files[]` names 7. The two test files appear only in `tests[]`, which carries a per-file case list and is not the same instrument. `tests[]` for forecast/app.test.ts names three cases, none of them the third test shipped ('stays suppressed when an active filter excludes the posted transaction'); `tests[]` for transactions.test.ts names six of the twelve shipped. Four cases beyond those lists: the misnamed category case, the two overshoot cases, and 'still splits out when one child of an under-filled split is unsplit'. Three are load-bearing — the overshoot cases pin the second commit's overrule, exactly the decision that should have had an acceptance criterion.

Fix: Either list both test files in `files[]` with the cases actually shipped, or record the deviations (extra cases, flipped expectation on the partly-typed case) in the PR description.

`packages/loot-core/src/server/forecast/app.test.ts:570`

Evidence: `createForecastWithSplitPostedOccurrence` wraps `startServices()` in a try/finally calling `stopServices()` and delegates to `buildSplitPostedOccurrenceForecast`; the two-function shape spans :570-583. The comment argues that a later case must not find `startServices` already called, which is what `beforeEach`/`afterEach` scoped to the block guaranteed for every case it contained, including the three shipped. The rewrite does make each test read `createForecastWithSplitPostedOccurrence(...)` rather than relying on block state — the one real gain — at the cost of a second function name and the comment.

Fix: Keep the hook pair and give each test a helper for the forecast construction only, or accept the two-function shape but cut the comment to the sentence that justifies it.
